name: h100
description: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 (GH100, Hopper, sm_90) at its 1980 MHz boost clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 132 SMs (SXM5), 64 resident warps/SM, 4 schedulers x 32 lanes (NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 50 MB L2 (whitepaper): 25 ways over power-of-two sets; 64 banks of 64 B, the power of two nearest the part's L2 bandwidth per clock (as a100)
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 5 HBM3 stacks x 16 64-bit channels at 5236 MT/s = 40 128-bit channel pairs, modelled as 32 at 6545 MT/s for a power-of-two interleave: 32 x 16 B x 6545 MT/s = 3.35 TB/s, the card's bandwidth; latency not calibrated
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_PEA: 1980 MHz boost clock, 3.35 TB/s (H100 SXM5 datasheet)
sources.FETCH_WIDTH: 4 SM processing blocks, each with its own warp scheduler, dispatch unit and L0 instruction cache (NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper)
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock per SM: 32 banks of 4 B on the part (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, shared memory). Vortex banks are XLEN wide (8 B), so 16 banks carry the same bytes per clock; lanes reading one 8 B word share its bank access, so a stride-1 FP32 warp read is conflict-free as on the part
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Every NVIDIA GPU since Pascal has a demand-paged MMU (unified memory), global and shared-memory atomics with a native compare-and-swap (atomicCAS), FP16 storage and conversion, and per-partition special-function units for the transcendentals (MUFU)
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE, TCU_*, EXT_DXA_ENABLE, E: Fourth-generation tensor cores: FP16/BF16, TF32, FP8 and INT8 (no INT4), 2:4 structured sparsity, warpgroup MMA (wgmma); the Tensor Memory Accelerator is the DXA (H100 whitepaper)
sources.xlen: 64-bit machine: 64-bit pointers and FP64 (the D extension follows XLEN=64), with a 48-bit device address space against NVIDIA's 49-bit virtual addresses; configure --profile picks a build64 tree and a build32 tree rejects the profile
sources.NUM_BARRIERS: 16 named CTA barriers (bar.sync 0-15, PTX ISA) on every NVIDIA GPU
sources.EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_OM_ENABLE: Off: the datacenter part is built for compute (no display outputs; the raster and ROP hardware is reduced or absent), so the profile models its compute machine
sources.NUM_MUFU_LANES: 16 special-function results per clock per SM (4 SFUs in each of the 4 processing blocks) for the reciprocal, reciprocal square root, log2, exp2, sine and cosine (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 9.0)
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: GH100 SM (H100 whitepaper, Figure 7): 4 processing blocks, each with 32 FP32, 16 INT32, 16 FP64 cores, 8 LD/ST units, 1 SFU and 1 tensor core. One Vortex ALU/FPU/LSU block per processing block (ISSUE_WIDTH=4) with the part's INT32, FP32 and LD/ST lanes; a 32-thread warp instruction issues over NUM_THREADS/lanes cycles, as on the part. The TCU stays full-warp (NUM_TCU_LANES == NUM_THREADS). FP64 is not modelled separately: with XLEN=64 each FPU lane also executes FP64, so the profile has 128 FP64 lanes per SM against the part's 64
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO, FCVT_PE_R: 16 results per clock per SM, 4 per processing block: FP32 reciprocal and reciprocal square root, on which division and square root are built, and the 32-bit type conversions (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput); 32 FPU lanes / 8, compute capability 9.0
sources.DCACHE_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock of L1 data per SM: 4 banks of the 32 B dcache word. The default (one bank per LSU request channel) gives 8, twice the part
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE, DCACHE_SIZE: 228 KB maximum shared memory per SM (CUDA Programming Guide, compute capability 9.0) in a 256 KB window. DCACHE_SIZE keeps the whole 256 KB L1/shared pool: the driver gives a kernel the L1 its shared-memory use leaves
